Nonheterantherous stamens do not imply globally integrated architecture: S. lycocarpum is andromonoecious, with hermaphroditic and functionally male flowers. Pollen is the sole floral reward; anther presence strongly increases visitation, pollen availability falls rapidly under bee visitation, and visitor size/behavior determines stigma contact and single-visit fruit production. These source-resolved observations establish competing pollen-removal versus gamete-transfer fates without inferring conflict from architecture. The broader architecture is therefore coded as among-flower module division rather than shared integration.
Natural and manipulative evidence distinguishes feeding and pollinating anther functions; case-defining conflict/architecture evidence is direct.

Isomorphic equal/subequal stamens and hymenopteran visitation are source-resolved, but a broader BALANCE architecture mode cannot be assigned from these sources alone. A matched pollen-removal/allocation experiment testing reward-versus-gamete conflict has not been recovered.

Amorim et al. 2017 directly tested division of labour in S. alata using floral-organ measurements, artificial sonication, field bee interactions and species-specific division-of-labour experiments. Pollen from middle/feeding positions is routed to bee regions accessible for collection, whereas pollen assigned to the pollination route is directed toward less groomable transfer sites. This upgrades pollen-fate conflict from UNRESOLVED to POSITIVE without relying on heteranthery morphology alone.

This control remains source-secure as nonheterantherous under the frozen morphology gate: seven fertile stamens are equal in size and shape, with three sterile staminodes. Independently, Amorim et al. 2017 directly tested S. spectabilis and showed positional pollen routing through deflector-petal ricochet and division of labour among flower structures. Thus heteranthery is absent while within-flower functional division and pollen-reward versus transfer routing are present; the control is POSITIVE for pollen-fate conflict rather than globally integrated.

Luo et al. 2009 directly observed female Xylocopa buzzing the short feeding stamens, with vibration causing pollen from the long pollinating stamens to form a cloud on the bee's dorsal abdomen while the stigma contacted the same pollen-covered region. This directly separates bee-accessible reward collection from gamete-transfer routing. Higher viability in long-stamen pollen and later short-stamen enrichment in bee-relevant lipids/proteins provide independent functional support. Conflict is therefore POSITIVE without treating morphology alone as evidence.

The control is source-secure as a nonheterantherous VIIb taxon with direct bee buzz-pollination observations. Nonheteranthery is not treated as proof of globally shared integration or weak pollen-fate conflict, so broader architecture and control-side conflict remain UNRESOLVED pending matched functional evidence.
